locator.section: 9.4 Esters, 'Aliphatic methyl esters' (the one-line scheme labelled alpha)

evidence.curator_note: ARC COUNT (convention D), measured by me at 14x on the native 1760x2560 scan: the precursor carries EXACTLY TWO arcs, both single-barbed fishhooks, and their heads CONVERGE on the same empty gap between the CH2 and the alpha carbon -- i.e. on the FORMING C=C pi bond. Arc 1 (the long one) has its tail descending onto the R-CH2 sigma bond; arc 2 (the short one) has its tail at the radical dot on the alpha carbon. Moves <1,2> are those two arcs. Move <3> is NOT drawn: the second R-CH2 electron leaving on R, which is what actually produces the 'R.' the page prints as the first product. The reaction arrow itself is a plain labelled 'alpha' arrow with no arc. This is the canonical radical-site beta-scission (the book's 'secondary beta-bond cleavage'), and the product is conjugated -- the new C=C sits next to the C=O+ -- which is exactly the 'conjugated EE+ ion' the prose promises: the ion is EVEN-electron (charge +1, no unpaired electron) while the precursor was odd-electron. GENERIC SCHEME -- THE INSTANTIATION IS THE CURATOR'S AND IS SPELLED OUT. Equation 9.33 is printed as a single condensed line at the bottom of printed p254 carrying THREE generic labels: 'R-CH2C(.)R'a-C(OH)=+OR --alpha--> R. + CH2=CR'a-C(OH)=+OR'. Nothing is named, no m/z is printed and no compound is drawn out. The licensing prose is three lines above it on the SAME page: 'If an R_alpha group is ethyl or larger, secondary beta-bond cleavage can give a conjugated EE+ ion (Equations 9.33, 8.79).' That sentence is what constrains the choice: the group whose bond cleaves, R-CH2-, must be ETHYL OR LARGER, so R = CH3 is the minimum. The subsection is 'Aliphatic methyl esters', so the ester alkyl OR is taken as OCH3, and the second alpha substituent R'a -- printed as a group label, not as an H -- is taken as the smallest alkyl, CH3. INSTANTIATION CHOSEN: precursor CH3CH2-C(.)(CH3)-C(OH)=O(+)CH3, C6H12O2+., curator-computed 116.0832; product ion CH2=C(CH3)-C(OH)=O(+)CH3, C5H9O2+, 101.0597; neutral CH3. (15.0235). EVERY mass in this record follows from that choice, not from the page. A reviewer preferring the cross-referenced Equation 8.79 literally would set R'a = H (precursor C5H10O2+. 102.0675, ion C4H7O2+ 87.0441); the graph would be the same shape. ATOM MAPS: 1 = the carbonyl carbon (bearing OH and the charged ester oxygen), 2 = the alpha carbon (the radical site), 3 = the CH2, 4 = R (the methyl expelled), 5 = R'a, 6 = the hydroxyl oxygen, 7 = the charged ester oxygen, 8 = its methyl. WHAT THE PRECURSOR IS: not a molecular ion. It is an ODD-ELECTRON DISTONIC FRAGMENT -- charge drawn on the ester oxygen as '=+OR', radical drawn as a dot on the alpha carbon -- i.e. the ion that arrives from the delta-/epsilon-hydrogen migration plus 1,4-hydrogen shift described in the prose immediately above (and it is the charge-on-the-ester-oxygen partner of the resonance pair IMS9-EQ9.32a stores for its m/z 74 ion). ms_context.adduct is therefore null, NOT '[M]+.' (convention G).

data/mechanisms/rule_index.json has NO chapter-9 entries. UNTESTED, not 'no rule matches': no MOD rule was searched for or tested against this record, because the precursor is a generic curator-instantiated distonic fragment rather than a molecular ion, so any embedding count would describe my instantiation and not the page. The closest family by shape is hTransition_unsaturated_alpha (IMS_bookCover.py:50), which performs the same radical-site beta-scission with alkene formation, but its LHS requires the [_A+][H] protonated form of the carbonyl and this precursor's charge is drawn on the ester oxygen instead; that mismatch was reasoned from the DFS string, not measured, and is recorded as such.
